issues.legal_issue: The applicability of later amendments to a general acquisition law to acquisitions under a separate enactment incorporating that law, and the resulting lapse of analogous acquisition notices.
material_facts: The acquisition was made under a separate enactment that incorporated provisions of the earlier general land acquisition law.
The appeal challenged the refusal of relief on the basis that a later amendment caused the acquisition notification and declaration to lapse after two years.
Earlier decisions of the Supreme Court had held that the later amendment did not apply to acquisitions under the separate enactment.
issues.conclusion: The later amendment does not apply to acquisitions under the separate enactment, and the analogous notification and declaration do not lapse after two years under that amendment. The High Court was right to refuse the claimed relief.
issues.legal_principle: Where provisions of a general enactment are incorporated into a separate enactment, subsequent amendments to the general enactment do not automatically apply to the separate enactment. The Court treated the issue as settled by Gaurishankar Gaur v. State of U.P. [(1994) 1 SCC 921], U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad, Lucknow v. Lata Awasthi [(1995) 3 SCC 573], and Ramesh Chandra Tiwari v. U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad, Lucknow (decided January 8, 1996). It therefore held that the amendment's two-year lapse provision did not apply.

predicates.appeal_from_denial_of_acquisition_relief: A party appealed after a court refused relief concerning an acquisition.
predicates.special_enactment_incorporated_earlier_l: The acquisition proceeded under a separate enactment that incorporated provisions of an earlier general acquisition law.
predicates.later_amendment_invoked_to_claim_notice_: A party relied on a later amendment to the general law to claim that acquisition notices had lapsed.
predicates.precedent_excluded_later_amendment: Earlier controlling decisions had treated the later amendment as inapplicable to acquisitions under the separate enactment.

issues.definition: When an appeal follows denial of acquisition relief, the acquisition proceeded under a separate enactment incorporating an earlier law, a later amendment is invoked to claim that notices lapsed, and earlier controlling decisions exclude that amendment, the amendment-based lapse claim is rejected.
